tagline: An old tavern beside the road to Concord.
intro: From Cambridge, Route 2 runs through Arlington and Belmont toward Lexington, then continues through Lincoln to the Concord Rotary. The freeway gives way to a road with traffic lights. Parts of Route 2 are still known as the Cambridge and Concord Turnpike.

The neighboring buildings keep several different centuries. Lexington has modern houses fitted to the hills of a former peacock farm; in Lincoln, Hoar Tavern faces the highway from behind sound barriers and a low stone wall.

moments.title: Peacock Farm
moments.text: In Lexington, split-level houses follow the hills of a former peacock farm, whose old farmhouse and barn remain at the development entrance.

moments.title: Hoar Tavern
moments.text: Behind sound barriers beside Route 2, the clapboard tavern faces the road that follows the colonial turnpike.

moments.title: Dr. John Cuming House
moments.text: At Elm Street and Reformatory Circle, a timber-framed house recalls the physician who left Harvard a bequest for a medical school.
